elevator_pitch: ~(bWhere Code Meets Color: Mathematical Art at Any Age~)b
Mathematics and software development filled my professional life for decades.
Now, in retirement, those same worlds find a new expression.
Equations, algorithms, and code become the paintbrush—transforming into images filled with color, rhythm, and harmony.
Every piece grows out of curiosity, experimentation, and a lifelong passion for structure.
This work is living proof that mathematics is never cold, but vibrant and full of life.
Welcome to my space. Enjoy the journey through the beauty of numbers.

full_story: Born in Greece, with an early fascination for numbers and shapes.
A natural path led me to mathematics, revealing that
behind every formula lies a form, and behind every form, a small story.
Decades of professional life were devoted to programming—writing code, solving problems,
and building systems with logic and precision as primary tools.
Retirement did not close a chapter, but opened a fresh one.
Thus, two great passions—~(bmathematics and programming~)b—merged into something entirely new: generative art.
Through equations, fractals, randomness, and algorithms, programs are written that *paint*.
Rules are defined, parameters tuned, and the code is left to surprise even its creator.
Often, a small change to a single number completely transforms the result.
Every image becomes a dialogue between logic and imagination, where the rigor of numbers meets the freedom of color.
I am an amateur artist. Deep enjoyment drives the entire process.
Hours spent experimenting, trying, failing, and trying again shape each piece until the final image emerges.
This website presents a curated selection of work.
May it spark a shared feeling: that mathematics is not merely knowledge,
but beauty, and that art can be born where least expected—deep inside a line of code.

artworks.title: Spiral heart filled with indian red color
artworks.alt: Heart-shaped spiral of nested red outlines filled with a soft indian red color
description:
The parametric heart curve is a timeless and elegant piece of mathematical art.
In its standard form, it is defined by the following system of equations:
~(i  x = 16 * (sin(t))^3 ~)i 
~(i  y = 13 * cos(t) - 5 * cos(2*t) - 2 * cos(3*t) - cos(4*t) ~)i 
~(i  (with t taking values in the interval [0, 2*pi]) ~)i 

To achieve the mesmerizing visual result you see in the graphic,
a few creative adjustments were introduced to the base formula: 
~(b*Coefficient Tuning*~)b: Subtle modifications to the constants to balance the proportions and symmetry of the heart.
~(b*Spiral Growth Factor*~)b: Multiplying each equation by a scaling factor dependent on ~(it~)i, 
which causes the curve to dynamically expand outward as the angle progresses. 
~(b*Extended Domain*~)b: Expanding the domain of ~(it~)i into higher multiples of ~(i2*pi~)i, allowing
the lines to wrap around continuously and form the intricate, layered spiral effect.

artworks.title: Phyllotaxis Twist
artworks.alt: Spiral of small hearts radiating from the center, shifting from deep purple to orange and pale yellow
description: In botany and mathematics, the term ~(b<phyllotaxis>~)b describes how nature arranges petals or seeds around a stem.
This phenomenon is modeled by Vogel's spiral, where each element is placed using the Golden Angle (137.5°)

and a sublinear radius 
 ~(i   (r = c * sqrt(n)) ~)i  
 to ensure maximum packing density.
This artwork introduces a deliberate geometric twist.
While preserving the Golden Angle for the rotation,

the radius function is transformed into a linear one: 
  ~(i   r = c * n ~)i
This shift alters the geometry into an Archimedean spiral.
Instead of nature's compact scaling, the linear progression forms distinct visual spokes radiating outward.
Along this path, each coordinate is occupied by a heart that gradually increases in size,
creating a captivating dialogue between rigid mathematical structure and organic emotion.

artworks.title: Mathematical quadruple tweaked Archimedean spiral
artworks.alt: Four overlapping curved shapes in red, green, blue and orange, each made of many fine parallel lines and rotated by 90 degrees
description:
The Archimedean spiral is one of the most iconic curves in mathematics.
In its natural polar habitat, it is defined by the equation 
   r = a + b * θ 
When translated into parametric equations, its fluid motion is captured by: 
  x(t) = (a + b * t) * cos(t) 
  y(t) = (a + b * t) * sin(t) 
But what would happen if we replaced cos(t) with, for example, cos(2t)? 
What if we experimented with the frequencies and constants? 
In short: what happens when mathematical precision meets digital experimentation
and we begin to <<tweak>> the formulas? 
In this piece, we explored that exact curiosity through a two-step creative process: 
1. The Transformation: By creatively altering the parametric core equations, we disrupted
the spiral's classical balance, forcing the curve to fold into an entirely new, unexpected geometry. 
2. Chromatic Symmetry: We rendered the resulting curve four times using four distinct colors.
Each layer is rotated by 90 degrees relative to the previous one, building a hypnotic interplay of fourfold rotational symmetry.
A digital tapestry where geometry becomes the canvas, and equations turn into brushstrokes.

artworks.title: A Silent Symphony of Mathematical Whispers
artworks.alt: Symmetrical looping curve with a red outline and gold fill, forming a knotted, ribbon-like figure
description: This digital artwork was born from the rigorous precision of mathematics, utilizing
parametric and trigonometric equations combined with integrals to define its curves.
Visually, the composition exudes a unique elegance, where the vibrant red outline dynamically
bounds the gold fill, creating a sense of perpetual motion against a transparent background.
The symmetrical curves weave together a harmonious balance that bridges science with aesthetics.

artworks.title: Geometric Mandala with Harmonic Wave Patterns
artworks.alt: Circular floral pattern of overlapping white loops forming a ring with a smaller circle inside
description: This artwork originates from parametric mathematical equations, combining sine
and cosine functions modulated by distinct frequency parameters.
Through a precise algorithmic process, numerical constants are converted into a continuous,
fluid geometric trajectory across the digital canvas.
The visual outcome reveals a striking floral structure that
seamlessly balances mathematical rigor with organic elegance.
Overlapping lines construct a subtle illusion of depth and movement,
yielding a minimalist yet dynamic aesthetic.

artworks.title: Psychedelic Chaos - Entangled Waves
artworks.alt: Large double spiral of purple, red and white bands, with a psychedelic wave pattern entering from the left
description: This digital artwork is a mathematical representation of complex patterns.
Generated using trigonometric functions on a Cartesian grid, it is rendered
through contourf plotting, transforming numerical values into visual forms.
The main part is dominated by a striking double vortex, while on the left it
intertwines with a psychedelic wave produced by trigonometric functions.
The color gradients enhance the sense of motion and energy, giving the artwork an ethereal
yet scientific aesthetic that harmoniously blends mathematics with digital art.

artworks.title: Geometric Triple Vortex Brick LineArt
artworks.alt: Triple spiral vortex made of fine terracotta-colored brick-like marks that follow flowing curved lines
description: This digital artwork is driven by a fluid dynamics algorithm,
where the contour lines of a triple vortex are mathematically calculated
and converted into automated structural design elements.
The result is a mesmerizing mosaic of terracotta bricks that
faithfully follow the fluid gradient of the flow.
In areas of intense curvature and turbulence, the mortar joints tighten,
creating an impression of density and dynamic tension.
Rigid geometry seamlessly merges with organic motion,
transforming abstract equations into a vivid,
earthy texture that evokes the feeling of an ancient, moving mosaic.

artworks.title: Triple vortex on a wavy surface (ver 01)
artworks.alt: Triple vortex of fine contour lines in green, cyan, red, magenta and blue, with a bright multicolored center
description: The artwork takes shape digitally on a grid of points, emerging through
the interaction of mathematical functions and angular fields.
Successive transformations guide the numerical values, rendering
the structure through subtle contour lines.
Three vortices form at the center, surrounded by undulating orbits and smaller swirls.
The composition appears to undergo a quiet metamorphosis,
creating a dense yet balanced visual field.
The color palette shifts from greens and cyans to reds, magentas, and blues,
where the tonal transitions impart a soft sense of rhythm, motion, and depth.

artworks.title: Triple vortex on a wavy surface (ver 02)
artworks.alt: Triple vortex of fine contour lines shifting from deep blue and cyan through green to yellow and red
description: This piece represents a new exploration on the digital grid,
where subtle shifts in the transformation parameters redefine
the geometry of the angular fields.
The contour lines trace a new structural path, capturing
a distinct equilibrium of mathematical forces.
At the center, three vortices and adjacent swirls rearrange into smooth, flowing orbits.
The color gradient shifts seamlessly from cool deep blues and cyans, through mid-tone greens,
to warm yellows and reds, imparting a natural sense of fluid motion, balance, and quiet depth.

artworks.title: The Pulse of Earth
artworks.alt: Three groups of curved terracotta-colored lines arranged in a rotational pattern around the center
description: This artwork was algorithmically generated using contour plotting techniques
based on parametric functions and coordinate meshes, seamlessly translating
complex mathematical equations into dynamic geometric forms.
Dense, flowing lines intertwine into an abstract organic composition,
evoking a sense of pulsating movement and spatial depth.
The rich terracotta tone infuses the piece with earthy warmth, striking
a captivating balance against its precise mathematical origins.
Set against a transparent background, the sweeping curves breathe freely,
guiding the viewer's focus to the rhythmic flow, intricate structure, and
harmonious dialogue between algorithmic precision and artistic expression.

artworks.title: Truchet tiles with curved colored lines (ver 01)
artworks.alt: Truchet tiles with curved two-colored arcs forming circles and S-shaped paths in bright colors
description: This artwork was generated algorithmically based on classic Truchet tiling
over a 4X4 geometric grid, where each individual tile features
randomly oriented, double-layered curved arcs.
Through random orientation and a vivid ten-color palette, the piece transforms
a rigid geometric layout into a continuous, dynamic visual flow.
The curved forms connect seamlessly across boundaries, giving birth
to a lively, vibrant labyrinth that beautifully balances structural order
with artistic spontaneity.

artworks.title: Minimalist Axe-Head Motif: Algorithmic Tiling Symmetry
artworks.alt: Grid of axe-head shaped tiles in dark teal, orange, red and green, randomly rotated to form a mosaic
description: The algorithm operates on a structured grid layout, generating a matrix of individual cells.
Each cell renders the complex ~(i<<axe-head motif>>~)i geometric shape,
precisely defined across multiple intersecting circular arcs.
The final visual artwork harmonizes mathematical rigor with controlled randomness.
As the fundamental tile undergoes random rotations and draws colors from a rich,
earthy palette, an organic mosaic emerges.
The sweeping curves connect and interplay across adjacent cells,
transforming a rigid grid into a fluid, mesmerizing pattern reminiscent
of contemporary generative tiling art.

artworks.title: Butterfly, using transformations of <<Circular Coordinates>>
artworks.alt: Symmetrical butterfly whose wings are made of rippling, multicolored curved stripes
description: This artwork captures a butterfly through the prism of an alternative geometric universe.
Its visual form is based on <<Circular Coordinates>>,
a theory introduced in the journal The Mathematics Teacher (1971)
and developed for computer designs by Tanis and Kuivinen in Mathematics Magazine (1979).
Unlike classical polar or spherical coordinates,
circular coordinates are not a simple polar transformation from radii and angles,
but a complex geometric system based on families of circles.
~(iThe Axes~)i: There are two orthogonal axes, U and V.
~(iGeometric Construction~)i: Each point on the axes acts as the center of a circle
that necessarily passes through the origin (0,0).
~(iPoint Definition~)i: A point (u,v) in the new system is defined as the intersection of the circle
whose center is located at u on the horizontal axis with the circle
whose center is located at v on the vertical axis.
Through this mathematical transformation function,
the natural symmetry of the butterfly is reconstructed,
blending rigorous geometry with organic art.
To compose complex and symmetrical designs,
such as the form of a butterfly, families of curves are utilized.
By adding a constant c to a simple function g(u), that is
~(i   f(u) = g(u) + c ~)i
and applying the algebraic transformation of circular coordinates,
straight lines morph organically,
producing striking, kaleidoscopic geometric patterns.

artworks.title: Tangent circles with holes
artworks.alt: Spiral of internally tangent circles in green, orange, yellow, teal and pink, shrinking toward a small blue dot
description: This digital artwork is built on a precise geometric sequence of internally
tangent circles, with each consecutive radius decreasing by a fixed factor.
The mathematical complexity deepens as the tangency point of each circle shifts
spirally by ~45 degrees from the previous one, generating a dynamic rotational trajectory
Visually, this minimal composition comes alive through a vibrant, curated color palette
featuring hues like limegreen, orange, and gold, contrasted by every third circle being transparent.
The result is a hypnotic interplay of depth and transparency, where rigid
geometry transforms into a fluid, multi-layered visual experience.

artworks.title: Organic Curved Voronoi Mosaic Pattern (no 51A2)
artworks.alt: Abstract mosaic of curved tiles in orange, green and blue, separated by pale turquoise borders
description: The artwork is based on the mathematical structure of Voronoi diagrams, transforming
the conventional geometry of polygonal tiles into a system of curved regions.
The original geometric boundaries are smoothed using a Gaussian filter, producing
fluid curves and naturally rounded connections between neighboring areas.
Visually, the result resembles an abstract mosaic of organic, flowing tiles.
The curved joints create a sense of continuous movement, while the multicolored palette
combines warm and cool tones, giving the composition balance, depth, rhythm, and visual energy.

artworks.title: Minimalist Organic Charcoal Voronoi Abstract Geometry (no 67M1)
artworks.alt: Abstract mosaic of curved tiles in shades from charcoal to near white, separated by soft gray borders
description: Rooted in the mathematical logic of Voronoi diagrams, the work transforms a precise
geometric structure into an organic, almost fluid landscape.
Its boundaries are softened through Gaussian smoothing, allowing the underlying
geometry to acquire a sense of continuity, softness, and natural movement.
Spanning a palette from deep charcoal to near white, the curved surfaces
create a quiet interplay of light and shadow.
The composition balances order and freedom, resembling an abstract mosaic
that seems to shift and transform continuously, inviting the eye
to wander through its flowing network of forms.

artworks.title: Magma Julia Fractal Chaos Art (seed 99319)
artworks.alt: Julia set fractal with purple spirals glowing against a black background, with bright pink-orange centers
description: This digital composition depicts a Julia set fractal,
which is based on the iterative application of complex functions.
For this specific artwork, the classic equation form
~(i f(z) = z^2 + c ~)i was used.
It is worth noting that beyond this baseline formula, the field includes other
mathematical variations, such as alternating between different
constants (c1 and c2), raising to higher powers, or incorporating trigonometric functions.
The visual structure develops into symmetric spirals around two main centers,
with smaller, self-similar substructures repeating infinitely.
The magma color palette was applied for the visualization.
Deep black and purple dominate the artwork, while the centers of the spirals are highlighted
with bright colors, showcasing the system's convergence points.
